findings.title: Duplicate function bodies in cache.rs tests (293/309)
findings.description: Two test functions share a 147-node body once names and literals are set aside. Both are test helpers that seed an in-memory SQLite cache and query by source id.
findings.trigger: Future schema or query changes require touching every twin — easy to miss one and let it drift.
findings.suggested_fix: Factor the seed-and-query sequence into a private test helper (`fn seed_then_query(...)`) and call it from both tests; the assertion is the only line that needs to stay bespoke.

findings.title: Duplicate function bodies in cache.rs tests (375/390)
findings.description: Two test functions share a 122-node body. Both are short helpers that seed two entries and assert query result ordering.
findings.trigger: Schema or query semantics change → both must be updated in lockstep.
findings.current_code:
#[test]
fn upsert_is_idempotent_by_id() { ... }
#[test]
fn upsert_then_query_by_category() { ... } // structural twin
findings.suggested_fix: Extract the seed-and-query scaffolding into a private helper; keep each test's distinct assertion inline.

findings.title: Byte slicing may panic in sanitize_generated_at — column 19-30
findings.description: `bytes[0..4]` is range-indexed on the sanitized wire bytes. The earlier `bytes.len() < 20` guard makes this safe today, but the dependency between the guard and the slice is implicit.
findings.trigger: A future refactor that loosens the length guard without updating the slice bounds would crash on a short wire value.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `bytes.get(0..4)` / `.get(5..7)` / `.get(8..10)` and `return None` if any slot is missing; makes the bound explicit and impossible to drift.

findings.title: Byte slicing may panic in sanitize_generated_at — column 33-44
findings.description: `bytes[5..7]` is the day-of-month slice; same implicit dependency on the length guard as HB-003.
findings.trigger: Same as HB-003 — any drift between the length check and the slice site is a latent panic.
findings.current_code: for slot in [&bytes[0..4], &bytes[5..7], &bytes[8..10]] { ... }
findings.suggested_fix: Replace with `bytes.get(...)` so the length check is encoded in the slice expression itself.

findings.title: Byte slicing may panic in sanitize_generated_at — column 47-59
findings.description: `bytes[8..10]` is the day-of-month slice (third slot).
findings.trigger: Same as HB-003/HB-004.
findings.current_code: for slot in [&bytes[0..4], &bytes[5..7], &bytes[8..10]] { ... }
findings.suggested_fix: Same `.get(...)` migration as HB-003/HB-004.

findings.title: Four near-duplicate function bodies in official_mcp.rs (174/191/257/271/273/289/291/302)
findings.description: Four functions share ≥81% of their body once names and literals are removed. They differ only in the entry id they look up and the assertions on the resulting `ExtensionEntry`.
findings.trigger: Adding a new preset projection (e.g. when `presets::catalog()` gains a new shape) requires touching every twin in lockstep.
findings.suggested_fix: Build a shared `fn assert_projection(entries: &[ExtensionEntry], id: &str, expect: impl FnOnce(&ExtensionEntry))` helper that locates the entry and routes to a per-test closure carrying the bespoke assertions.

findings.title: Two near-duplicate filter chains in origin.rs (349/359 and 361/370)
findings.description: The `exact` and `leaf_matches` branches in `forget_installed` are structurally identical except for the predicate: `o.local_ref == backend` vs `local_ref_addresses(&o.local_ref, backend)`. Both then `.map(|o| o.entry_id.clone())` and `.collect::<Vec<String>>()`.
findings.trigger: Adding a third matching mode (e.g. partial-path) would mean copy-pasting a third time.
findings.suggested_fix: Extract a `fn collect_entry_ids<'a>(rows: impl Iterator<Item = &'a InstallOrigin>, pred: impl Fn(&InstallOrigin) -> bool) -> Vec<String>` helper and call it twice.

findings.title: Indexing `candidates[0]` after a `len() == 1` guard in reconcile.rs
findings.description: `Some(candidates) if candidates.len() == 1 => Some(candidates[0].enabled)` — the guard makes this safe, but clippy::indexing_slicing does not thread pattern guards and flags it as a potential panic.
findings.trigger: Cosmetic; cannot actually panic today. Future clippy changes could escalate it.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `candidates.first().copied().map(|c| c.enabled)` or `candidates.iter().next().map(|c| c.enabled)` to side-step the lint without changing semantics.

findings.suggested_fix: Build a `fn assert_reconcile(catalog: Vec<ExtensionEntry>, installed: Vec<ExtensionEntry>, origins: &[InstallOrigin], expect: impl FnOnce(&[ExtensionEntry]))` helper.

findings.title: Four duplicate test helper bodies in reconcile.rs (279/315/332/452)

findings.title: Two near-duplicate test bodies in trust.rs (218/237 and 239/259)
findings.description: ≥85% similar. The two `stdio_runs_commands_and_requires_ack` / `official_oci_no_ack` tests share the same scaffolding (build `mcp_entry()`, mutate, call `build_disclosure`, assert).

findings.title: Cross-module near-duplicate between trust.rs:272 and memory/scratchpad/manager.rs:1060
findings.description: ≥83% similarity between a test in `trust.rs` and a test in `memory/scratchpad/manager.rs`. They differ in the input string under scan but the assertion pattern is identical.
findings.trigger: The two test families will drift independently when the SSOT's invisible-char list is extended.
findings.suggested_fix: Lift a shared `fn assert_scan_flags(text: &str, expected_kinds: &[&str])` into `security::unicode_guard` (or a new `security::test_helpers` module) and reuse it from both call sites.

findings.title: TOCTOU between sha256 verify and copy in install_git_skill
findings.description: `install_git_skill` computes the digest via `verify_plugin_integrity(&src_leaf, sha256.as_deref())` and then calls `copy_skill_leaf(&src_leaf, &staging)` outside of any lock. A local actor with write access to `skills_dir/.git-cache/<mcp_server_id(entry.id)>/<leaf>` can swap the directory's contents in the window between verify and copy, defeating the sha256 pin and installing attacker-controlled bytes under the trusted digest. The pin is the load-bearing security control here (per the comment block at line 119), so this is the right surface to harden.
findings.trigger: Local-user or co-tenant write access to `~/.aleph/skills/.git-cache/...`; not remotely exploitable in the default install path but exploitable if `skills_dir` ever lands in a world-writable location (shared CI, container with a volume mount).
findings.suggested_fix: Either (a) hold the existing per-checkout `Arc<Mutex<()>>` from `clone_or_update_at` (currently scoped to the clone call only) across verify + copy, or (b) re-stat and re-digest the source under an open file handle (`O_NOFOLLOW` + `openat`-style walk) immediately before the copy, or (c) atomically rename `.git-cache/<id>` aside, hash inside a snapshot, then `rename(2)` back. Option (a) is the smallest diff and matches the existing single-flight design.

findings.title: sanitize_generated_at accepts digits at the timezone-open slot
findings.description: At position 19 (the byte after the `T...:...:...` time block), `is_date_or_time_field` is false so the inner check is skipped and only `is_accepted_elsewhere` applies. Because `is_accepted_elsewhere` includes `b.is_ascii_digit()`, a wire value like `2026-07-30T00:00:00<digit>5:34:56Z` (a digit inserted where `+`/`-`/`.`/`Z` is required) survives the slot check. The downstream `SyncReport.generated_at` is then displayed verbatim. Lower-risk than full bypass — the field is *displayed*, not executed — but the structural check is leaky at exactly the position its name says it's strict.
findings.trigger: A hostile publisher can ship an RFC3339-shaped value that renders as a long digit run, defeating the per-slot intent.
findings.suggested_fix: Restrict position 19 (and position 20 if present) to exactly `b'.' | b'+' | b'-' | b'Z'`; do not allow arbitrary digits at the TZ-open slot.

findings.title: forget_installed exact-match branch lacks the ambiguity guard that leaf-match has
findings.description: When `exact` is non-empty, `forget_installed` deletes *every* matching row without checking how many there are. The leaf-match branch correctly warns and returns 0 when the leaf is shared by multiple rows; the exact branch does not. Two catalog entries that legitimately installed into the same MCP server id (e.g. an old preset id being replaced by a Hub id with the same slug via manual reinstall) would both be wiped on a single `extensions.uninstall` call.
findings.trigger: Race or operator mistake that produces two `install_origin` rows pointing at the same `local_ref`; or a future code path that mints ledger rows with a duplicate `local_ref`.
findings.suggested_fix: Mirror the leaf-match guard: `if exact.len() > 1 { warn!("ambiguous exact match"); return Ok(0); }`. The single-match case keeps the current fast path.

findings.title: scan_for_injection lowercases the full input twice per entry
findings.description: `scan_for_injection` calls `stripped.to_lowercase()` and `nbsp_replaced.to_lowercase()` on the *entire* input before iterating `SUSPICIOUS`. For a catalog with N entries and M phrases, that's 2*N allocations + 2*N*M substring searches on every sync. With 1000 entries × 16 phrases, 32k `String::to_lowercase` calls. The phrasing lowercasing can be moved inside the needle loop (`needle.to_lowercase()` is 16 cheap allocations, not 1000).
findings.trigger: Cold catalog sync over a large artifact (catalogs grew with the official MCP preset set); also runs per-entry on every sync.
findings.suggested_fix: Lowercase the *needles* once at module load (e.g. `static SUSPICIOUS_LC: &[&str]` built from `SUSPICIOUS.iter().map(|s| s.to_lowercase()).collect()`) and only lowercase the input once (strip invisibles AND replace NBSP into a single pre-lowercased buffer). `SUSPICIOUS` is short enough that a `OnceLock<&'static [&'static str]>` makes this constant-time.

findings.title: mark_installed_state is O(catalog × installed) per call
findings.description: For each catalog entry, `installed.iter().find(|ie| ie.id == expected)` (MCP branch) and `by_name.get(&key)` followed by `candidates.iter().find(|c| ...)` (other branches) scan linearly. The Plugin/Skill branches already build a `HashMap`, so the MCP branch is the only one that's linear. For a 1000-entry catalog × 200 installed backends that's 200k comparisons per reconcile, on a path called by every `extensions.*` RPC and the `hub_catalog_search` tool.
findings.trigger: Large installed sets + large catalog (the design point of the hub).
findings.suggested_fix: Build a `HashMap<&str, &ExtensionEntry>` over `installed` once at the top of the function (keyed by façade id) and reuse it from the MCP branch; the Plugin/Skill branches can keep their existing `by_name` map.

findings.title: Error chain dropped via `.map_err(|e| e.to_string())` on the install path
findings.description: `mcp.add_server(cfg).await.map_err(|e| e.to_string())?` flattens a `McpError` (or equivalent) into a `String`, losing the typed error and its source chain. The agent-side handler surfaces the string verbatim in the install reply, so on failure the operator sees the rendered message with no way to programmatically distinguish a spawn failure from a config validation failure from an upstream refusal.
findings.trigger: Any non-Ok path through `run_install`'s McpStdio/McpRemote branch.
findings.current_code: mcp.add_server(cfg).await.map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
findings.suggested_fix: Either return the typed error up (`Result<InstallOutcome, McpError>`) or use `anyhow::Error` / `Box<dyn std::error::Error + Send + Sync>` so the original error chain survives the boundary.

findings.title: matches_query allocates a fresh lowercased string per field per row
findings.description: For each entry matched against the catalog query, `matches_query` calls `e.name.to_lowercase()`, `e.description.to_lowercase()`, every `t.to_lowercase()` for tags, and `a.to_lowercase()` for author. With 1000 entries and a 4-field query, that's 4000+ `String` allocations per query. The lowercase form could be cached on `ExtensionEntry` (compute once on insert into the cache) since the row's data column is the JSON-encoded entry.
findings.trigger: Hot search paths on large catalogs.
findings.current_code:
e.name.to_lowercase().contains(&q)
    || e.description.to_lowercase().contains(&q)
    || e.tags.iter().any(|t| t.to_lowercase().contains(&q))
    || e.author.as_deref().is_some_and(|a| a.to_lowercase().contains(&q))
findings.suggested_fix: Add a derived `name_lc` / `description_lc` / `tags_lc` / `author_lc` (or one packed struct) that lives next to the row and is computed once on `upsert_entry`; `matches_query` then becomes substring checks against precomputed haystacks. Same trick the existing `name_lc` index column already uses for SQL `ORDER BY`.

findings.title: mcp_server_id does not sanitize characters other than ':' and '/'
findings.description: `entry_id.replace([':', '/'], "_")` only rewrites two characters; everything else (spaces, `'"\``, control chars) survives verbatim. The hub catalog already rejects empty / non-`local:` ids in `HubCatalogArtifact::validate`, but a future schema change that loosens the id charset could let weird ids through and produce a server id that the McpManager (and downstream filesystem consumers) interpret in surprising ways.
findings.trigger: Future catalog schema changes; not exploitable today given the existing validator.
findings.suggested_fix: Run the result through the same `sanitize` from `secrets.rs` (or a stricter `[A-Za-z0-9_-]+` whitelist) so the contract is "the output is a safe server id regardless of input shape", not "we only translate two delimiters".

findings.title: Hardcoded catalog URL with system-CA trust
findings.description: `ALEPH_HUB_URL = "https://hub.heyaleph.com/catalog.json"` is a single hardcoded trust anchor with no certificate pinning and no key transparency fallback. `safe_fetch` is the right tool (SSRF-defended, body-capped), but the entire catalog's integrity rests on the system CA store + DNS. If the publisher's CA is compromised, every consumer fetches the attacker-controlled catalog; the trust-tier clamp in `ingest` prevents self-promotion but does not prevent distributing attacker-written entries at any tier below `Verified`.
findings.trigger: CA compromise, DNS poisoning against the system resolver, or a `safe_fetch` SSRF policy regression that re-enables a redirect to a private IP.
findings.current_code: pub const ALEPH_HUB_URL: &str = "https://hub.heyaleph.com/catalog.json";
findings.suggested_fix: Out of scope for the hub module (URL is a deployment concern), but the architectural note is: pair this URL with a per-build catalog SHA-256 (like Chromium's component updater) so the URL is just a transport hint and the digest is the trust anchor. Surface the expected digest in an `ALEPH_HUB_EXPECTED_SHA256` constant and verify before `ingest`.

findings.title: .git-cache persists across installs with stale origin URL
findings.description: `install_git_skill` keys the cache by `mcp_server_id(&entry.id)` (the catalog entry id) but `clone_or_update_at` uses the *existing* checkout's `origin` remote on subsequent calls, not the URL passed in. The first install with `git_url = "https://github.com/X/Y"` poisons the slot; a later install from a different catalog entry id (or after a catalog republish that points to a new URL under the same id) will fetch from `X/Y`, not the new URL. The note at line 215 acknowledges the disk-leak but does not acknowledge the URL-pinning side effect. The catalog validator's `entry_count`/`trust_tier` checks do not catch this because the URL is per-spec, not per-artifact.
findings.trigger: Catalog republish that retargets an existing entry id; manual cache directory manipulation by a local actor.
findings.suggested_fix: When the catalog entry's `git_url` differs from the existing checkout's `origin`, wipe the checkout before re-cloning (or refuse the install with a typed error). Either treat the catalog's URL as authoritative or fail closed. This also makes the GC story in the comment at line 215 well-defined — "no current install" == "no checkout at all".
